issues.legal_issue: A tenant’s comprehensive covenant to maintain leased premises and execute repairs at its own expense attracts the restricted repair deduction when the owner undertakes only major repairs.
material_facts: The owner leased a house under a covenant requiring the tenant, at its own expense, to maintain the premises in good, habitable and tenantable condition and execute all repairs, including repairs to electrical and sanitary fittings.
The owner undertook at its own cost major repairs such as repairs against collapse of the house.
In reassessments of the rental property, the tax authority treated the tenant’s covenant as bringing the repair deduction within the provision applicable where a tenant bears the cost of repairs.
issues.conclusion: The tenant had undertaken substantial repairs, and the owner’s separate undertaking concerning major repairs did not share the burden of those repairs. The deduction was therefore governed by Section 24(1)(i)(b), not Section 24(1)(i)(a), and was limited accordingly.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 24(1)(i)(b) of the Income-tax Act, 1961, where a tenant has undertaken to bear the cost of repairs, the owner’s repair deduction is limited to the amount specified by that clause; Section 24(1)(i)(a) does not apply instead. A repair covenant requiring a tenant to keep premises in tenantable, habitable or good repair can require substantial repairs. Repair may include replacement or renewal of a subsidiary part, including restoration of its stability or safety, but reconstruction of the entirety need not be repair. The Court relied on Halsbury’s Laws of England, 14th edition, paragraphs 285 and 286; Lurcott v. Wakely and Wheeler; Rodesia Railway Ltd. v. Income-tax Collector; and Ravenseft Properties Ltd. v. Davstone (Holdings) Ltd. It distinguished Commissioner of Income-tax v. Parbutty Churn Law on the facts.

predicates.rental_property_income_assessment: The proceeding concerns the assessment of income from property leased to a tenant.
predicates.tenant_covenant_requires_comprehensive_r: The tenant agreed to maintain the premises in good, habitable or tenantable condition and to execute all repairs.
predicates.tenant_must_pay_repair_costs: The tenant agreed to pay the costs of the repairs it undertook.
predicates.owner_undertakes_only_major_collapse_rep: The owner undertook at its own expense only major repairs, such as repairs against collapse.

issues.definition: When a rental-property income assessment involves a tenant who must pay for comprehensive repairs while the owner undertakes only major collapse repairs, the repair deduction is limited to the category applicable to repairs borne by the tenant.
